findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox items instead of plain lines
findings.description: All five `**Commit**:` markers (lines 96, 179, 249, 286, 325) are written as checklist items (`- [ ] **Commit:** ...`). The marker convention requires plain lines, never checkboxes — which is also the house style in every other task file in `project-documents/user/tasks/` (e.g. 301-tasks, 302-tasks, 303-tasks use bare `**Commit**: ...` lines while their steps remain checkboxes). Wrapping markers in checkboxes makes them indistinguishable from actionable steps and muddies the "working, tested point" semantics. Placement itself is correct: one marker per section after tests pass, not after every task and not deferred to the end. Fix is to de-checkbox the five marker lines.

findings.title: Task 3.5's named call-site list is inaccurate but covered by its catch-all
findings.description: The step names `tests/test_force_builder.py` and `tests/test_clients.py` as likely `SimulationManager` constructors. Verified: `tests/test_clients.py` contains no `SimulationManager(...)` construction, while `tests/test_repulsor_integration.py:53` does and is not named. The "or any other file" catch-all instruction does cover it, so nothing is left unmet, but naming `test_repulsor_integration.py` explicitly (and dropping `test_clients.py`) would reduce the chance a hurried implementer fixes only the named files.

findings.title: Frontmatter `status: complete` conflicts with unchecked checkboxes and Task 5.3
findings.description: The task file declares `status: complete` (and the slice design does the same) while every checkbox remains `- [ ]`, and Task 5.3 (lines 312–313) still instructs the implementer to set `status: complete`. Whichever artifact is stale — the status field (if this is a plan awaiting work) or the checkboxes (if the work is done, per CLAUDE.md's "check off after completing" rule) — one should be reconciled so readers can tell what is actually done. This does not affect the breakdown's coverage or sequencing.
